2026 SEMA Show • 2027 Dodge Charger Gets Special-Edition Package Celebrating 90 Years of Mopar
Peanut Butter Is a Bamboo-Filled Camper Van With a Cozy Interior Built for Off-Grid Adventures
49 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Levity Vans
Bamboo is a really popular material for camper van conversions. However, it's rare to see a conversion that has as much bamboo as the project I'd like to share with you folks today – meet Peanut Butter.
What we have here is a build based on a 2022 4x4 Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 144" wheelbase. It was created by Levity Vans, a Santa Cruz, California-based company that specializes in transforming cargo vans into high-end adventure machines.
As always, let's start the tour by taking a look at the exterior. The van's exterior is quite telling, not hiding the fact that this is a camper van – it doesn't "scream" camper van either, as it doesn't have a myriad of upgrades like we see on other projects.
The van rides on black Sprinter wheels wrapped in Kumho Crugen all-season tires. At the rear, you'll come across an Owl Vans spare tire carrier, as well as a bumper step.
On the roof, you'll come across a Fiamma manual awning and a 400 W solar array. Other notable exterior mods are side steps, Rolef bug screens, and a set of flares.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Levity Vans Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are super common on Sprinters because this model is narrower compared to other popular camper base vehicles, like the Ram ProMaster or the Ford Transit.
Flares are designed to increase the van width to allow you to fit a bed inside in an east to west arrangement instead of the standard north to south setup. This rig's Vanspeed capsules have been color matched to the van's paint and come with half-slider windows.
Stepping inside, you'll immediately feel the warm embrace of the bamboo design. Of course, making the entire interior with bamboo would've probably been an eye-sore. In this van, all the cabinetry was made out of bamboo plywood, as well as some other elements, such as a headliner shelf.
The rest of the design consists of walls upholstered in light grey fabric, a soft tan ceiling, and wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring. The look is complemented by some stainless steel elements, like the cabinet and drawer handles or the sink faucet, as well as a black solid surface countertop.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Levity Vans A key detail is that the interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. This layout is a must on small-wheelbase vans like this Sprinter, as it helps make the living space feel roomier.
The driver and passenger seats are mounted on swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van and used after you've set up camp.
This front seating area continues further back in the form of a Bellagio bench seat offering room for two people. It comes with seatbelts and armrests, but the best part about it is that it can be folded flat and raised out of the way, to the side. Moreover, the seating area is completed by a large Lagun table mount that can be easily removed. By the way, the elements in this space were added after the video tour and photos of the van were taken.
Next, we have the kitchen, which is split into two units, one on each side of the living space. It features a deep stainless steel sink with a cutting board insert and a separate filtered water faucet, a microwave oven, a large Isotherm Cruise 130 12V fridge with a tiny freezer compartment, and a single-burner induction stovetop.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Levity Vans A flip-up table extends the standard 36 inches (91 centimeters) of meal prep area to a total of 55 inches (139 centimeters). Moreover, a Maxxair vent fan is perfectly positioned above the induction stove to draw out the smells and fumes from cooking.
Three overhead cabinets, four drawers with soft-close mechanisms, and two lower cabinets are available for storage. One of the lower cabinets houses a composting toilet and has two flip-up panels that can double as steps to get into bed.
Finally, the rear part of the living space is taken up by a fixed bed arrangement that's 79.5 inches (202 centimeters) long and 60 inches (152 centimeters) wide. You'll also notice two overhead cabinets, charging points (both USB and standard outlets), and two reading lights with a red function that's ideal to use at night.
The bed platform is positioned quite high up, making room for a large garage underneath. It offers abundant space in the middle, while its sides are taken up by two tall boxes – they integrate storage compartments and accommodate the utility systems. The bed platform and the two boxes are also made out of bamboo ply.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Levity Vans To make loading and unloading items in the garage easier, the builders fitted a pull-out tray. It's attached to heavy-duty slides that can support up to 500 lb. (227 kg) and has an L-Track that allows you to secure gear or large items. The garage is definitely tall enough to accommodate a mountain bike, provided you remove the front wheel.
Power is on the left side - the electrical system's highlights are a 300 Ah BattleBorn battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter. Furthermore, you can use solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging to keep the batteries topped off – if used correctly and cleverly, it's possible to never run out of juice.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 27-gallon (102-liter) freshwater tank, an 11-gallon (41-liter) greywater tank, and an outdoor shower connection with a pull-out sprayer. Both water tanks are mounted underneath the vehicle, and the greywater one can be dumped at the flip of a switch thanks to an electronic dump valve.
The last important system in this rig is a Rixen's hydronic heater that provides both heated air and hot water.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Levity Vans The "command center" for the rig's utilities is integrated onto the side of one of the kitchen overhead cabinets, conveniently located by the entrance. It includes four dimmer light switches, a battery monitor, an inverter controller, a thermostat for the Rixen's heating system, and switches for a garage light and a water pump.
All in all, the Peanut Butter build by Levity Vans has the right blend of fine aesthetics and home-like functionality.
When I started researching this camper van, I was bummed to discover that Levity Vans is no longer in business. I say bummed because it's sad to see that companies who create awesome homes on wheels go out of business due to financial reasons.
Levity Vans operated for a total of 9 years, but it was not able to continue operations due to the changing market and various financial pressures. Still, I feel like its creations deserve some attention. Stay tuned, as I'll be taking a look at other of its builds here on autoevolution.

2026 SEMA Show • 2027 Toyota Crown Signia Gets GT-S Concept Treatment for SEMA, Becomes a Sleek Wagon
Porsche Mission S Gets Visited by the Tuning Fairy – Rendering
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | a.c.g_design
Porsche may be indeed chasing after the money-making segments with all kinds of models that would have seemed impossible for the Zuffenhausen brand until a few years ago, but the company also remains committed to the driver-oriented part of the automotive game with several exciting products.
Here, must obviously name the 911 series, which remains successful, and comprises so many models that one can either deem it a sports car or a supercar, depending on the configuration. The upcoming 718 Boxster and 718 Cayman are also in the making as we speak, and while they were initially supposed to debut as EV models solely, the automaker has changed its mind, after seeing that electric vehicles have started losing ground.
Sticking an ICE unit, probably with some partial electrification, behind the passenger compartment is not enough to do the trick, because Porsche is reportedly not satisfied with how the two cars behave. Thus, it is back to the drawing board, more or less, and that’s why the upcoming 718 series still hasn’t debuted. The latest information suggests that the new Boxster and Cayman might enter production either in 2027 or maybe in 2028.
Now, Porsche hasn’t had an extremely powerful model in its lineup since the 918 Spyder. The spiritual successor to the iconic Carrera GT fought the likes of the Ferrari LaFerrari and McLaren P1, and it saw the light of day between 2013 and 2015 at the Stuttgart factory in Germany. It featured a 4.7-liter V8 assisted by two electric motors for a total of 874 hp (886 ps/652 kW) and 944 lb-ft (1,280 Nm) of torque.
Photo: Instagram | a.c.g_design Back then the 918 Spyder was deemed a hypercar, and it was capable of pushing from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) in just 2.6 seconds, hitting the 124 and 186 mph (200-300 kph) marks in 7.2 and 19.9 seconds, before topping out at 214 mph (345 kph). Its successor was previewed by the Mission X, an electric study presented more than three years ago (mid-2023), and the production model was initially supposed to go down the EV route.
However, just like in the case of the new 718 series, Porsche changed its mind, and that’s why we now have the Mission S. The latter concept was recently shown to the world, and it sticks to the ICE recipe. For whatever reason, the automaker decided not to detail the oily bits, stating only that it is “a mid-engine sports car platform positioned above the 911 – not as a one-off hypercar, but as a permanent and versatile addition to our customer offering,” as CEO Michael Leiters said.
Porsche’s new Mission S Concept looks like a more advanced 911 at the front, and features an intricate and quite cool (this writer believes) design at the rear, especially with the 917-inspired radiator fan, the flowing rear wing, and the quite uncommon diffuser.
As you already know, this machine has fallen into the hands of the pixel-altering crowd ever since before its grand unveiling. That’s because it was first imagined based on a leaked video, and subsequently, a few wheelmakers wanted a piece of the pie, so they sketched it out on various alloy sets.
Fast-forward to this week, and the Porsche Mission S has been envisioned yet again, this time with an emphasis on the tuning game. It was @a.c.g_design on Instagram who is responsible for the pixel-altering game in this case, which imagines the one-off machine with a more aggressive overall design.
We can see that it has a bigger air intake in the middle of the bumper, a much chunkier splitter, some flaps on the sides of the front bumper, and some add-ons on the front hood. The side skirt attachments have also come from the aftermarket world, and we can see that the back end is home to a new diffuser, and a much larger wing.
Shod in sticky tires from Michelin, the wheels are also part of the CGI makeover. They feature a Y-spoke design, have a brushed silver look, and are pretty much as large as the OEM ones. The Porsche Mission S is now presented in blue instead of white, and it still features quite a few black accents on the outside.
Now, this makeover is definitely on the controversial side of things, in my opinion, anyway, because the car in question looks very aggressive without any outside intervention, not to mention that it is an eye-catching product. But it is still interesting to see what it could look like if it were to go down this route, and to be honest, I’d rather have the regular concept with no mods whatsoever. I also hope that the final production model will stick to this design, because it is a very cool machine.
But do you like the pixel-altered product envisioned here, or would you rather have the regular Porsche Mission S with zero mods? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Λutomotive Custom Garage (@a.c.g_design)

Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 Heritage Searching for a Deep-Pocketed Enthusiast on the Used Car Market
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | seraj.garage
Does the Shelby GT500 version of the S550 Ford Mustang still keep you up at night? Well, we won’t judge if it does, because this is a one extremely exciting muscle car.
And if you said yes, and you probably have, as you are here reading these lines, and looking to find out more about the pictured example, then you may want to keep reading, because the machine you see above in the gallery is for sale in the United States of America, with a used car dealer behind the ad. And it does not only look very good, but it is also a Heritage Edition.
As you probably know, the S550 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 usually costs between $75,000 and over $110,000 in today’s used car market Stateside, whereas the Heritage Edition + Carbon Fiber Track Pack, and this example has both, tends to get a lot more expensive. For instance, something like this tends to go between $120,000 and over $155,000, depending on the mileage and overall condition.
Yes, you read that right, the pictured muscle car is not only a Heritage Edition, but also benefits from the Carbon Fiber Track Pack. It rides on carbon fiber wheels, to absolutely no one’s surprise, which spin around the red brake calipers that feature white Brembo branding. It also features the usual body kit expected from a GT500, has white dual racing stripes, a large wing sitting on the trunk lid, and four big exhaust tips sticking out from the rear.
Photo: Instagram | seraj.garage On the inside, this Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 has leather and Alcantara upholstery. The interior is mostly black, but a few white accents provide some contrast. We can see them on the seats, center console, and even on the steering wheel, in the form of a 12 o’clock marker. White stitching is also on deck, and so is the carbon fiber trim. Some metal accents can also be seen here, and the Recaro bucket seats boast the famous Shelby Cobra logo in white.
We can see a bit of wear on the driver’s seat outer bolster, and that is not exactly a surprise, because this machine is not really a garage queen. You are looking at a 2022 model year, according to the vendor, and at the time of cataloging, it had a little over 13,000 miles on the clock. In fact, the odometer read 13,268 miles (21,353 km), to this muscle car has seen some action. But it still looks very good both inside and out, this writer thinks, and there is no doubt that it will attract a petrolhead in no time.
However, that depends not only on the car’s overall appearance, mileage, and other factors, because the asking price also plays a decisive role. And you are probably curious how much this one is. But we will keep this information close to our chest for the moment, as in the meantime, we also have to delve into the oily bits, as it is these that have made the S550-generation Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 famous.
Photo: Instagram | seraj.garage The muscle car has a supercharged 5.2-liter V8 engine under the hood in this configuration, which was rated at 760 hp (567 kW/771 ps) back when the vehicle was still found in dealer lots nationwide. The thrust was 627 pound-feet (847 Nm), and this enables it to hit 60 mph (97 kph) in just a little over three seconds from naught. You are looking at a 10-second car, as the standing quarter mile takes 10.7 seconds, according to the spec sheet.
And that makes it even more exciting than the lesser Mustangs from that era, doesn’t it? It also allowed the Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 to sit neck and neck with those pesky Hellcats from Dodge, that challenged (pun intended) it to countless drag races. And we should also name the Chevy Camaro ZL1, which is dead and buried, and might return as a four-door sedan, perhaps with a V8 engine, and maybe a manual transmission option.
Now, we told you everything that we know about this 2022 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500, which is a Heritage Edition that boasts the Carbon Fiber Track Pack, and has a little over 13,000 miles on the odometer, and it is definitely a lot more than the vendor said in the social media post embedded at the bottom of the page. The dealer is known as @seraj.garage on Instagram, and says that it accepts trade-ins, offers financing, and can ship this machine nationwide.
But how much would you have to fork out if you wanted this Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 parked in your driveway? That would be $104,995, according to the ad, and it’s definitely not bad at all for something like this, is it? If you were shopping for an S550 GT500 and came across this one, would you make it yours for $105K? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Seraj Abughoush (@seraj.garage)

2026 SEMA Show • Honda Racing Releases Its First-Ever In-House Made Parts for the Civic Type R and Integra Type S
The Encore Is a Beastly Truck Camper With All the Luxury, Now for Sale for an Eye-Watering Price
63 photos
Photo: Rossmonster
I've seen few truck camper builds that are as extensive and adventure-ready as those from Rossmonster. Today, I'm checking out a "pre-loved and pre-built" rig, as it calls them, that's looking for a new owner – I'll tell you more about pricing at the end of the article so as not to shock you straight away.
Meet Encore, a project that's based on a 2025 Ram 5500 Crew Cab with a 4x4 drive. As I mentioned, it was created by Rossmonster, a Longmont, Colorado-based company that transforms trucks and vans into incredibly capable homes on wheels.
When it comes to truck campers, Rossmonster offers two options: the Baja Trail and the better-equipped Baja Plus – the Encore is, as expected given how it looks, part of the latter category.
The company made sure to make the Encore trail-ready – and not just fit for simple trails, but also for more hardcore off-roading. The stock Ram 5500 can already handle going off the beaten path – this one is powered by a 6.7-liter Cummins turbo diesel engine outputting around 360 hp and 800 lb-ft. (1,084 Nm) of torque.
However, the builders added all the right options to improve the off-road capability. First off, the vehicle rides on 20-inch raw aluminum wheels wrapped in Michelin X Force ZL rough-terrain tires.
Photo: Rossmonster I also love how this wheel and tire combo fits in aesthetically, with the aluminum rims pairing nicely with the blue vehicle body and the grey camper box. The camper box is a custom composite frame sitting over an aluminum frame. Furthermore, the entire vehicle is coated in Raptor truck bed liner for an extra layer of protection.
Second, the truck is equipped with a Liquid Springs suspension – it's a fully active, smart hydraulic suspension system that replaces a truck's factory leaf springs, coil springs, and shock absorbers.
Instead, it uses a compressible silicon fluid combined with computer microprocessors to dynamically alter the truck's spring rate and damping in real time, 1,000 times per second. It also has a Tru-Earth Leveling system, which levels the truck automatically by adjusting each hydraulic strut on its own.
At the front, you'll come across two ditch lights and a massive Hammerhead bumper complete with D-Ring recovery points, a Warn winch rated for 20,000 lb. (9,071 kg), and an integrated Baja Designs clear LED light strip.
Photo: Rossmonster On the opposite end, there are additional useful accessories: a spare tire carrier and two carriers holding cargo boxes with adjustable shelving and Molle panels on the side. Underneath, you'll discover a custom Rossmonster Baja bumper with a backup camera, Rigid scene lights, an ARB air compressor, and a hitch receiver.
I saved the most significant exterior mod for last: a gigantic elevating roof. At the touch of a button, you can raise the camper box's roof to create a ton of additional room inside. By doing this, you'll also reveal several windows. When you're driving, it stays low to reduce height, improve clearance, and minimize wind resistance.
Rossmonster put the roof space to great use. It installed four solar panels with a total capacity of 760 W, a Fiamma awning, two Maxxair vent fans, and a Nomadic Cooling X3 A/C unit.
Before we take a look inside, I wanted to mention that Rossmonster even put the cab to good use. It removed the rear passenger seat arrangement and replaced it with a storage platform providing multiple compartments. Moreover, it added a 4-camera system and a Garmin screen for navigation. A nice touch is that a door lets you pass from the cabin to the living space and vice-versa.
Photo: Rossmonster Other notable exterior mods are traction boards attached on the passenger side, a large Molle panel, running boards for the cab that have integrated hammock pole mounts, powered steps for the camper box, and power and water connections.
The contrast between the exterior and the interior couldn't be more drastic – you move from a rugged exterior to a warm and welcoming interior packed with luxuries.
Regarding aesthetics, you'll notice walls upholstered in grey tweed fabric, white oak slab-door cabinets, and wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring. The look is complemented by white Corian Platinum solid-surface countertops, black leather upholstery for the seats, and a custom topo backsplash (topo as in it imitates the pattern of topographic maps).
Dead ahead as you enter, Rossmonster created one of the most sought-after camper van facilities: a bathroom. Hidden behind a conventional white oak door, it boasts a shower with a handheld wand, a Thetford cassette toilet, a teak floor insert, and a removable hanging rack.
Photo: Rossmonster Next, we have the kitchen on the passenger side. It features an Isotherm Cruise 200 stainless steel fridge with a freezer compartment, a two-burner induction stovetop, a microwave oven, a deep sink with a folding faucet and a cutting board cover, and a multi-function Panasonic oven. Counter space is arguably quite limited, but you get two flip-up tables that create more surface area.
On the opposite side, you'll come across a massive storage unit. It offers three large drawers, a pull-out pantry, a small counter, and a huge fridge/freezer.
The rear part of the living space is taken up by a lounge area. It has a U-shaped couch and a large table in the middle. You can drop the table to the same height as the couch, rearrange the cushions, and transform this area into a comfy sleeping arrangement for the guests.
Several overhead cabinets follow the same shape as the couch and provide plenty of room for storage. What's more, above, the builders fitted a Maxxair vent fan.
Photo: Rossmonster Three benches make up the couch. Besides offering a bit more space to store your items, they accommodate the utility systems.
The electrical system's highlights are a 1,200 Ah battery bank paired with a 3,000 W inverter/charger. Three charging sources are available: solar power, shore power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running.
As for plumbing, the rig is equipped with a 40-gallon (151-liter) freshwater tank, an additional 25-gallon (95-liter) freshwater tank underneath the vehicle, an under-mounted greywater tank, and a single-stage water filtration system.
The last important systems in this rig are a Nomadic Cooling X3 A/C unit and a Rixen's MCS7 hydronic heating system that provides heated air and hot water. It also powers a radiant floor heating system.
Photo: Rossmonster You'll have to use a ladder by the rig's entrance to get into the bedroom, which is located above the driver's cabin. This is undoubtedly a comfier solution compared to the rear sleeping arrangement. It also has a Maxxair vent fan above, two reading lights, and two front-facing windows.
As I said initially, the Encore is now for sale . You'll need a fortune to be able to get your hands on it - $440,000 (€393,580), to be precise, as shared on its listing. It currently has 16,889 miles (27,180 km).
You could get a conventional house for that money, so it's only fair that some people will have a strong reaction to this price tag.
However, it's safe to assume that the target audience for such a creation won't be bound by a budget. And it's undeniable that this truck camper by Rossmonster is an awesome adventure machine that can take you off-road and keep you off-grid for long periods.

Nostalgic About 1990s Chevrolet and Ford Models? Here's a Fox Body and Suburban Digital Ointment
9 photos
Photo: the_kyza / Instagram
Khyzyl Saleem, the virtual artist better known as " the_kyza " on social media, is thinking that now is maybe the perfect time to play with old things. After all, the member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators hadn’t been dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI lately.
Instead, the pixel master embarked on a wacky adventure after he joined the 2K Tour, an adventure involving ten teams that get $2k each to buy and modify a car – then drive it across 1,500 miles of “challenges and chaos.” One of the competitors managed to acquire a “ridiculous” Chevrolet Suburban for $2k, which they then drove across California & back, and that wasn’t all that happened, since it was driven as if it belonged on the track.
“Did it belong on a track? No, absolutely not, but it sure inspired this thought of ‘what if’ it did!” So, the author set out to create ‘Big Red,’ a crimson Chevy ‘Burb that gives cheers to Scotty – aka Montgomery Scott, the fictional character in the science fiction franchise Star Trek that acts as Chief Engineer of the Enterprise ship from the original series and other entries of the franchise.
The CGI expert basically took an eighth-generation GMT400 Suburban and made it a slammed widebody track machine via a smooth aerodynamic body kit that includes a full widebody treatment along with a massive front spoiler and a large rear roof wing, among others. There are also bronze Rotiform six-spoke alloy wheels, massive track tires, a second wing for the dual rear doors, plus other ‘things.’
Those ‘other things’ include the new suspension setup, a set of bucket seats up front, and a complete roll cage inside, including in the massive trunk. What do you think? Yay or nay? By the way, that’s not the only suggestion for a bonkers 1990s-style transformation, as an earlier project concerns a yellow Fox Body Ford Mustang with an attitude, riding on “thick” tires and BBS E88s with a set of cool side exhausts and a full aerodynamic widebody kit as if it’s about to break a new quarter-mile dragstrip class record or something…
Of course, the current Chevrolet Suburban and Ford Mustang are a long way away from these 1990s-style builds. The General Motors SUV remains as hulking as ever at the top of the crossover and SUV roster of its Chevrolet subsidiary, starting from $63,700 and looking like it will never see the inside of a track unless it’s towing a dedicated ride.
The iconic Ford Mustang, meanwhile, is more and more a traditional sports car than a classic pony or muscle car, featuring the base EcoBoost turbo four-pot as an accessible option, but also the 5.0-liter Coyote V8 along with the 5.2-liter supercharged V8 on the Dark Horse SC and the ultra-expensive GTD. 12 photos
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago
There’s an entirely new supercar king in Lamborghini’s portfolio, and it’s not the Fenomeno . The latter is part of the brand’s few-off series, for whatever reason, it does not get that much attention. But its mainstream sibling, the Revuelto, does.
More often than not, a few examples of this model end up in our news feed weekly. Either due to a tuning job or the used car market. But this story has nothing to do with the Revuelto, but its predecessor, the Aventador. Made between 2011 and 2022, it gave birth to some extremely cool models, including the Veneno, Centenario, Essenza SCV12, Countach LPI 800-4, and Sian FKP 37, as well as the two Alston models, the SC18 and SC20.
On top of these, the Lamborghini Aventador was offered in the LP 700-4, SuperVeloce LP 750-4, S LP 740-4, SVJ LP 770-4, SVJ, and LP 780-4 Ultimae, among others. Ask any Lambo fan what their favorite Aventador is, and you will get different answers, though most of the time, petrolheads will mention the Super Veloce Jota (SVJ). This model debuted at the Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance back in 2018, boasting several improvements over the S and the SV.
It is a track-focused model and the first V12 Lambo to boast the ALA (Aerodinamica Lamborghini Attiva), so the aero upgrades were on deck, including the disconnected front splitter, a big carbon fiber rear wing with a central fin, a tri-dimensional air outlet on the hood, a large rear diffuser, and underbody vortex generators. The LDVA 2.0 (Lamborghini Dinamica Veicolo Attiva) management system is also on deck, thus further contributing to the car’s track-enhanced nature, and making it faster overall.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago The Lamborghini Aventador SVJ Roadster followed its fixed-roof sibling, being presented to the world at the 2019 Geneva Motor Show (the good old days!). It featured the same goodies, albeit with an open-top view of the sky above, consisting of a removable two-piece carbon fiber hard top. And if you dream about owning one of these, then you should know that the example shown in the gallery is looking for a new home in the United States of America.
This Italian supercar features a Grigio Liqueo exterior on top of a Nero Cosmus and Bianco Polar interior, and at the time of cataloging, it had in the region of 2,000 miles (3,200 km) on the clock. Thus, you are looking at an almost-new machine, despite being a 2020 model, and as you likely suspect, there isn’t anything wrong with it, as everything looks good, from the black Y-spoke alloys and green details, to the black leather and Alcantara upholstery, and the white contrasting elements on the inside.
You do know how much the Lamborghini Aventador SVJ Roadster unleashes at a hard push of the right pedal, don’t you? That would be 759 bhp (770 ps/566 kW) and 531 lb-ft (720 Nm) of torque, with the maximum thrust available at 6,750 rpm, and the peak output at 8,500 rpm. The 6.5-liter naturally aspirated V12 engine is mounted behind the passenger compartment, and works in concert with a 7-speed ISR, and a gen-4 Haldex all-wheel drive system.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago Despite its open-top nature, it is just as fast from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) as its fixed-roof sibling, as the acceleration takes 2.8 seconds. This makes it 0.3 seconds slower than the Revuelto, which uses a plug-in hybrid 6.5L naturally aspirated V12, with 1,001 hp (1,015 ps/747 kW) in total. The new Revuelto SV has 1,050 hp (1,065 ps/783 kW) to play with, and is 0.1 seconds faster than the standard Revuelto. As for the smaller Temerario, it hits 62 mph in 2.7 seconds, and has an electrified 4-liter twin-turbo V8 with 789 hp (800 ps/588 kW) in total.
Now, if you dream about owning a Lamborghini Aventador SVJ, then your pockets must be really deep, because this thing is on the extremely expensive side of things, regardless of the body style. For instance, the Roadster , which is the configuration of the pictured supercar, will set you back a minimum of $1.2 million in today’s market in the United States of America, and can easily exceed $1.5 million. Ultra-low mileage examples with less than 2,000 miles on the clock push past $1.6 million.
So, how much is the pictured Lamborghini Aventador SVJ Roadster? Unless you said $1,599,995, then you are wrong, because this was the asking price of the said supercar at the time of writing. You can find it in the possession of @motorcarsofchicago on Instagram, with the dealer stating that it accepts trade-ins and offers financing, and is not really fond of direct messages.
Thus, there you have it folks, if you have a $1.6-million budget and the desire to get one of these , then you know where you can find this supercar. By the way, a regular Lamborghini Revuelto will set you back over $610,000 new. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Motor Cars of Chicago (@motorcarsofchicago)

YouTube and Browsers Coming Soon to Android Auto, Google Says
12 photos
Photo: Google
The word “soon” certainly has a completely different meaning in the Google world. The search giant still claims that video apps, including YouTube, and browsers are still “coming soon” to Android Auto, something that the company has been saying since the spring of this year.
This time, it used the Android Dev Summit to highlight a table that we’ve all seen on the Android dev website and which includes the app categories supported by Android Auto and Android Automotive.
Video apps and browsers are both flagged as “coming soon” for Android Auto users, though no further ETA specifics were shared. Google originally promised that video apps would go live on Android Auto by the end of the year.
Video apps on Android Auto While YouTube has been around for quite some time in the Android Auto space thanks to third-party tools, Google wants to unlock the video app category officially with this upcoming update.
Once this happens, users will be able to watch videos on their infotainment screens when Android Auto runs without turning to any other methods. These applications, including YouTube , will only work when vehicles are parked for safety reasons. The video will be restricted once the vehicle starts moving.
These restrictions are already in place for the keyboard, where you are allowed to type only if you are parked. Once you begin driving, the keyboard is locked, so you need to pull over to type an address or rely on voice commands to continue driving and set up a new destination in the navigation app.
Photo: Mishaal Rahman on X Google wants to give users the ability to continue to listen to the audio track of a video, enabling video apps to switch to an audio-only mode if they support it. For YouTube, this would essentially trigger background play, meaning that you’ll need a Premium subscription to use this functionality in your car.
All the other video apps that want to be able to play audio when vehicles are in motion must support this audio-only mode.
Browsers are also coming to Android Auto, and users will be able to load websites just like they do on their phones directly from the infotainment screens. Browsers are already live on Android Automotive, so it’s safe to assume that the same applications will expand to Android Auto, including Google Chrome and Vivaldi. This experience will only be available for users when vehicles are parked, as indicated by Google’s table.
Browsers are still flagged as being in beta in cars with Google built-in.
What “soon” could actually mean for Google While Google hasn’t offered any specifics as to when we’re supposed to get video apps and browsers on Android Auto, the term “soon” could mean two things based on the previous Android Auto updates that used the same release schedule.
Last year, Google used the same term to announce the debut of Gemini , and the first users eventually received the update to the new AI-powered assistant in the last days of the year. The rollout then gained traction in 2026, with broad availability reached during the summer.
Photo: Google The Coolwalk update - the last major update for Android Auto - was originally supposed to go live in 2022, and Google repeatedly told users that it was “coming soon.” This didn’t happen, and while the Coolwalk update sporadically appeared in beta builds, it eventually started showing up for more users in the Android Auto beta program in late 2022.
Production devices started getting Coolwalk in the first quarter of the next year.
If Google uses the same approach, video apps and browsers could start showing up for beta users by the remaining weeks before December 31, while production devices - users who are not enrolled in the beta program - should start seeing video apps rolling out to their devices in the first quarter of the next year.
YouTube will probably pioneer the introduction of video apps on Android Auto, but more apps should follow. In cars with Google built-in, in addition to YouTube, users can also install streaming apps like Prime Video, with HBO also teasing an app that could eventually be able to run in the car.
Photo: Google Compared to Android Auto, where the apps running on the screen are controlled by your mobile device - and, therefore, must be installed on the phone to run on Android Auto - apps that support cars with Google built-in can be installed from a dedicated Google Play Store version running on the head unit. These apps, including YouTube and Google Chrome, can be found in the store.
On Android Auto, once YouTube and Chrome go live officially, these apps will appear on the infotainment screen once they are installed on your phone.
However, considering Google hasn’t yet shared any specifics on the release dates, we’d better not hold our breath because plans can always change. The third-party methods to enable YouTube on Android Auto continue to work, and unfortunately, some of them even bypass the restriction that locks the playing video to a parked state.
Via // 9to5Google

Tuned BMW M4 Goes Official With Unicorn Puke Livery
8 photos
Photo: Instagram | revozport
Is there anything that hasn’t been said about the second-generation BMW M4 ? Probably not. After all, this model blew six candles off its birthday cake this year, so it’s not exactly new anymore.
Moreover, it also underwent its first (and probably only) mid-cycle refresh, with the LCI, which means Life Cycle Impulse and is Bimmer slang for facelift, going official at the beginning of 2024. The LCI brought new lights, fresh wheels, some tweaks on the inside, and more power reserved for the top-of-the-line version, and is meant to keep this model on the competitive side of the class until its successor arrives, probably toward the end of the decade.
Word on the street is that the third-generation BMW M4 might arrive after 2029, because the current one’s production has been extended until that year. Chances are it will debut as a normal 4 Series first, with the full-blown M model joining the lineup eventually, and one does not need to be a BMW connoisseur to find out what it will look like, because all they have to do is look at the all-new 3 Series, which is a Neue Klasse model both inside and out, and rides on the an updated version of the old car’s CLAR platform.
The 4er is a slightly sportier take on the 3er, replacing the two-door body styles (coupe and convertible) versions of the F3X 3 Series, and also launching a liftback that is known as the Gran Coupe. The M4 Coupe and M4 Convertible are two-door versions of the M3, and the same will apply to the next generation.
Photo: Instagram | revozport But we are venturing a bit too far from the story here, so we will get back on track by stating the obvious: the M4 may not be new anymore, but it can still make headlines. And it is usually a tuned example that ends up in our news feed, or one that is searching for a new home on the used car market. This is a case of the former, and the tuner’s name behind the project is RevoZport .
The quoted company recently introduced some tuning kits for the F95 X5 M, the demised M8 Coupe, and the outgoing X6 M, and they were quite interesting, for the most part. And for what it’s worth, so is this BMW M4 Coupe, which features some of its visual extras on the outside. But the add-ons, which have likely been made of carbon fiber, are not the things that help it stand out, because that would be the livery.
As mentioned in the title, it definitely looks like unicorn puke, and it mixes what seem to be the typical BMW M colors on a white background, and with a very trippy pattern. The large front splitter, the side skirt extensions, the special trim on the front fenders, the rear diffuser, ducktail spoiler, and massive wing that sits on the trunk lid have all come from the quoted tuner’s portfolio.
And these are not the only things, because this BMW M4 Coupe is also wider than the standard one, though you may not be able to tell at first, and that is due to the trippy livery. The wheels do not look that special, and by that we mean that they do not seem to have come from the aftermarket world. But we could be wrong. After all, it’s not like we are wheel experts, and if we are indeed wrong, then please accept our apologies in advance.
Photo: Instagram | revozport RevoZport did not have much to say about this modified BMW M4 Coupe other than the fact that it features parts from its “Aero Kit,” and that it is “track ready.” There’s no doubt that this things will turn heads wherever it goes. After all, it’s not like it is a kitschy build, despite the livery, but what is your take on that?
Actually, before inviting you to answer in the comments section at the bottom of the page, we also have to mention the car’s oily bits, reminding you that all versions of the modern-day M4 (and not only) pack a 3.0-liter inline-six engine, with twin turbocharging.
The base BMW M4 Coupe has 473 hp (480 ps/353 kW) on tap. The mid-range M4 Competition Coupe is offered with 503 hp (510 ps/375 kW), and the top-of-the-line M4 Competition xDrive Coupe has 523 hp (530 ps/390 kW) available via the right pedal. The 0 to 60 mph (0-97 kph) acceleration is deployed in 4.1, 3.8, and 3.4 seconds, respectively, and for what it’s worth, the latter model is actually faster than the iconic Ferrari Enzo.
Pricing starts at $82,200 for the M4 Coupe, $86,400 for the M4 Competition, and $91,500 for the M4 Competition xDrive, and the M4 Competition xDrive Convertible has an MSRP of $98,400 attached to it in the United States of America. Double-Nostriled Dodge Hellcat Challenges the Used Car Market, Costs New Toyota Highlander Money
21 photos
Photo: Instagram | automotive_ambitions
Some muscle car enthusiasts are still waiting for Dodge to launch a V8-powered version of the modern-day Charger, because that still has not happened, even if this model will soon celebrate two years since it hit the assembly line north of the US border.
But such a thing is finally happening, presumably late next year for the 2028 model year, and the best candidate for the job seems to be the mighty Hellcat engine. You know, as in the mill that made over 700 horsepower in its most basic configuration, more than 800 horsepower on certain models, and a whopping 1,025 in its most potent guise under the hood of the Dodge Challenger Demon 170.
The latter remains the most powerful muscle car ever made and also the fastest, as it hits 60 mph (97 kph) in a very devilish 1.66 seconds. With E85 in the tank, it has 1,025 hp and 945 pound-feet (1,280 Nm) of torque to play with, and in perfect conditions, with a skilled driving sitting behind the wheel, it will complete the standing quarter mile in 8.91 seconds, at 151+ mph (243+ kph). Not bad for a bone-stock machine, is it?
Some might believe that the Hellcat engine is pretty much dead and buried today, but that’s wrong, because it is still a thing, and it powers the Ram 1500 SRT TRX and the Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat. And if everything goes well, then it will also make its way under the hood of the modern-day Charger. This would allow the latter to better rival the S650 Ford Mustang, and would also lift the bar for the upcoming Chevy Camaro, which is rumored to launch as a four-door sedan only.
Photo: Instagram | automotive_ambitions Now, while some enthusiasts are still waiting for Dodge’s modern-day muscle car to finally sit on the same step of the podium as the Ford Mustang, which is the only one in its class to be offered with V8 firepower today, perhaps joined by the rumored Copperhead (SRT), others continue to enjoy their V8-powered Challenger, or the old Charger. Or they’re probably dreaming about finally owning one of these, and if you are part of the latter category, then you may want to keep reading.
That’s because the muscle car pictured in the gallery is for sale in the States, and it is a Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat Redeye Widebody. The machine looks monstrous with its OEM double scoops on the grille, the factory widebody, the standard apron and ducktail spoiler, the SRT emblems, Y-spoke alloys, and so on. This one features an Octane Red exterior paint finish, and rides on glossy black wheels that spin around the red brake calipers.
On the inside, it features black leather upholstery with some white stitching for contrast, and also has some carbon trim, and the regular gear that this model was offered with. It is a 2021 model year car with a 220 mph (354 kph) speedometer, the listing reveals, the Plus Package, ventilated front seats, Driver Convenience Group, Laguna Leather Package, Laguna Leather Seats with SRT Hellcat logo, premium Laguna door trim panels, the Widebody Competition Suspension, an SRT Power Chiller, and a few other things.
Photo: Instagram | automotive_ambitions As for the firepower, it came from the ubiquitous Hellcat lump, a 6.2-liter supercharged V8 that was officially rated at 797 horsepower (808 ps/594 kW) and 707 pound-feet (959 Nm) of torque in this case. The engine’s peak output was available at 6,300 rpm, and the maximum torque at 4,500 rpm. The model hit 60 mph (97 kph) in roughly 3.5 seconds, completed the 1/4-mile in 10.8 seconds at approximately 131 mph (211 kph), and topped out at 203 mph (327 kph).
Sure, the power and the performance may not be up there with the mighty Dodge Challenger SRT Demon 170, but this 2021 Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat Redeye Widebody still offers more than enough oomph for daily drives. Not to mention that it can give real supercars a run for their money, while costing a fraction of their price. This one is said to have some 21,000 miles (~33,800 km) under its belt, and if you really want it, then you can park it in your driveway, after signing your name on the dotted line, and transferring the funds.
Speaking of the Benjamins, one should expect to pay between $55,000 and over $80,000 for a 2021 model year Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat Redeye Widebody in today’s used car market in the USA, and the latter number is for low-mileage examples that have less than 5,000 miles (~8,000 km) on their clocks. So, how much is the pictured muscle car? That would be $52,991, which is about as much as a new Toyota Highlander.
Interested parties should know that this one has an R-title, hence the asking price, and you can find it in the possession of @automotive_ambitions on Instagram. Is it worth the money in your opinion? View this post on Instagram A post shared by AUTOMOTIVE AMBITIONS (@automotive_ambitions)
